summary.one_liner: OpenHands Agent Canvas is a self-hosted developer control center for running coding agents (OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenCode, or any ACP-compatible agent) across local, Docker, VM, and cloud backends.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a web frontend for starting agent conversations and switching between multiple agent backends, such as a local machine, Docker containers, VMs, or OpenHands Cloud/Enterprise. It runs the open source OpenHands agent by default and can also drive third-party agents like Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, and OpenCode. An automation layer lets agents run on a schedule or in response to webhook events, with integrations named as Slack, GitHub, Linear, and Notion. The README gives examples such as publishing generated reports to Slack and decomposing GitHub issues into tasks. It can be launched via npm (@openhands/agent-canvas) or a Docker image, with options to split frontend and backend processes and to isolate each conversation in its own Docker container.
use_cases: Run coding agents on a personal laptop or a shared team server
Switch between local and cloud agent backends from one UI
Automate scheduled reports published to Slack
Turn GitHub issues into tasks automatically with an agent
Run several agents concurrently, each in its own Docker container
Use Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini CLI through a single control panel
how_to_run: git clone <repo> && cd OpenHands && npm ci && npm run dev
stack: TypeScript client for the Agent Server API
notable: Agent Canvas frontend can switch between multiple agent backends (local, Docker, VM, cloud) without losing focus
Supports any ACP (Agent Client Protocol) compatible agent, not only OpenHands
Automations run on a schedule or in response to webhooks, integrating with Slack, GitHub, Linear and Notion
Option to run each conversation in its own Docker container with persisted workspace and state
Local listeners bind to loopback by default, with explicit flags for LAN exposure
caveats: Default no-sandbox install runs the agent server directly on the host with full filesystem access
Requires Node.js 24 or later and uv; source builds pin npm 11.12.1
Windows setup is described in a separate README.windows.md rather than inline
Docker-per-conversation mode does not move the whole Canvas or automation service into a sandbox
keywords: run ai agents on a server
